parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a national universal-exposure document/visa regime — sex fixed at birth, X-marker ended, officers directed to refuse cases where records cast doubt on sex and to weigh lifetime fraud ineligibility, passports blocked, Supreme Court clearance, foreign travel advisories — with state layering: a birth-certificate facility rule covering all public and private schools and colleges (no enforcement mechanism, no recorded arrest), a minor gender-care ban of unresolved operative status, and a school outing mandate. Documented custody harm (immigration abuse, conversion-therapy prison policy) raises severity if detained. Offsetting: no criminalisation of trans identity, functioning courts that have enjoined provisions, federal hate-crime and employment protections, 33 municipal ordinances, no documented trans-specific violence. Compounding punitive provisions and official hostility preclude Reduced Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: National order bars self-selected markers; X-marker passports ended; Feb 2025 cable directs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility; travellers report confiscated/blocked passports and stranding; state motor-vehicle agency (Aug 2026) limits markers to M/F with exact-matching birth certificate or passport.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; litigation pending via civil-liberties union; a legal-aid FAQ advises on documentation and name/marker interactions.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at a consulate or crossing → refusal/fraud allegation → stranding abroad; state ID rules and federal marker rules reinforce each other.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Transgender men in immigration custody reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; from 2026 federal corrections mandate conversion-therapy-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal); a documented bathroom-trespass arrest elsewhere ended with 24 hours in a men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No criminalisation of trans identity here; the state facility statute carries no enforcement mechanism and no arrest or citation is documented under it; habeas and appellate review function.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy → investigation → possible federal custody, where birth-sex placement and hostile-practice policies apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State statute requires every K-12 school, college and university (public and private) to designate bathrooms, locker rooms and overnight accommodation by sex assigned at birth, with students required to match birth certificates; a national order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Statute has no enforcement mechanism and no documented case; single-occupancy restrooms exempt; 33 cities/counties bar gender-identity discrimination including public accommodations.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National funding leverage encourages compliance; a visiting minor at a school or campus encounters the designation directly.

care_services.exposure: SAFE Act bans puberty blockers, hormones and surgery for under-18s and bars trans girls from women's school sports; national order frames minor care as 'mutilation'; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records; proposed federal rule would bar insurance reimbursement for trans under-18s.
care_services.protection: State appeals court re-enjoined the SAFE Act (18 Mar 2025); 2024 proposed adult-care psychiatric-oversight rules were withdrawn and never took effect.
care_services.interaction: Adult travelling with a minor: provider chilling, refusal, and record exposure; operative status of the ban is unresolved.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy targets groups 'radically pro-transgender'; justice department guidance lists 'radical gender ideology' among extremist animating viewpoints; an order directs law enforcement to investigate schools and prosecute teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; a 2025 poll shows 66% backing sex-at-birth document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward memo expressly does not use 'radical gender ideology' as a criterion and states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing shapes officer discretion at screening, in schools and during any police contact.

minors_guardians.exposure: Facility law binds schools and colleges a visiting minor would use; a Jan 2025 law compels school staff to out LGBTQ students to parents; curriculum bans on 'gender ideology'; national order threatens criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; sports and care bans.
minors_guardians.protection: Facility statute has no enforcement mechanism or recorded case; care/sports ban re-enjoined March 2025; municipal non-discrimination ordinances in 33 cities and counties.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian travelling with a trans minor risks care denial, school exclusion and mandated disclosure of the child's status.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented. No trans-specific violence rate, pattern or incident in this state/province is sourced; a travel guide only advises checking recent violence reports.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gender-identity hate crimes punishable under the national hate-crimes statute; employment discrimination on gender identity prohibited nationally; no documented state-tolerated violence against trans people here.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Coverage is uneven: only 23 state/provinces have state-level gender-identity bias provisions.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Supreme Court allowed passport restrictions (Nov 2025); motor-vehicle marker rules announced without sourced rule text or effective date; facility-law practice, complaints procedures and county birth-certificate refusals unsourced; many measures remain in active litigation, so exposure varies by travel date.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts: 2020 ruling invalidated the birth-certificate ban; SAFE Act enjoined; EO provisions blocked; civil-liberties suit pending; legal-aid FAQ; federal appeal rights and municipal ordinances.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: A traveller's real exposure shifts with which measure is operative at the moment of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far below this anchor: 0.15-B involves routine border detention in crowded cells, tolerated assaults, withheld care and months-long habeas failures. Here detention is contingent, not routine; the state facility law carries no penalty or recorded arrest; no assault-in-custody pattern specific to this state is sourced. Custody abuse exists only in the national immigration/prison backdrop, not as everyday visitor exposure.

Closest structural match: routine document exposure at checkpoints, humiliation and denial-of-care documented, prosecutions of visitors uncommon, a narrow anti-discrimination claim with slow remedies and shifting official guidance. This dossier adds a nationwide visa-refusal/fraud lever and official hostility, but lacks the biometric-linked universal registry of 0.45-A, so slightly below it.

Materially lower: 0.75-C has trained border officers, acceptance of gender-congruent markers, written reasons, counsel access and compensation. Here the border regime deliberately refuses on sex doubt and considers lifetime ineligibility, states run a birth-certificate facility ban and a minor-care fight, and custody harm is documented — none of which 0.75-C features.

parsed.synthesis: For an adult alone, the operative regime concentrates risk at the border and in paperwork: the national document and visa regime is a universal exposure whose refusal and fraud consequences are enforced by the state itself and were upheld at the top of the judiciary; no amount of state-level municipal protection offsets it. On the ground, the state adds an unenforced but real birth-certificate facility rule, a contested minor-care ban and a school outing mandate, alongside federal hate-crime and employment protections, functioning courts and no documented trans-specific violence. Severity if detained is high because custody policies are documented as abusive. For an adult with a minor the exposure widens to school facilities, mandated disclosure and care denial, pushing the combined score into Elevated Risk rather than Reduced Risk.
